newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Busang collapse an embarrassment for Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Busang collapse an embarrassment for Indonesia.

text.p: The collapse of the Busang gold dream could not have come at a more embarrassing time for Indonesia in the midst of a general election campaign, political analysts said on Monday.

They said the government, and the Mines and Energy Ministry in particular, was likely to come under fire over the handling of the case, which an independent consultant on Sunday said involved the biggest fraud in mining history.

"You can expect acute embarrassment...it couldn't have come at a worse time right in the middle of the campaign," one analyst said. The next general election for the House of Representatives, held every five years, is due on May 29.

Adding to the embarrassment was the involvement of the Nusamba Group closely linked to President Suharto, which had moved in on Busang in February and quickly announced on Monday its withdrawal from the project.

For 30 months, the small Canadian mining firm Bre-X Minerals Ltd had issued mouth-watering estimates of the amount of gold at its Busang property in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province on Borneo island.
The frenzy reached a peak in February when Bre-X estimated reserves at 70.95 million ounces, which would have made it the biggest find of the century.

The dream turned into a nightmare in Canada on Sunday night when Bre-X released a report by consultancy firm Strathcona Mineral Resources Ltd that said an independent survey of the Busang site had produced no gold of commercial value.
It further said there appeared to have been fraud on an unprecedented scale.
Nusamba -- headed by close Suharto friend and adviser Muhammad "Bob" Hasan -- became involved following a bitter fight between Bre-X and Canadian gold giant Barrick Gold Corp for control of Busang.

Barrick bowed out and Bre-X retained a 45 percent stake in Busang. Nusamba ultimately got 25 percent, other Indonesian interests 15 percent, and Freeport McMoR=an Copper and Gold 15 percent and the job of developing the mine dependent on an exhaustive survey of the property.
Freeport, along with Nusamba, said on Monday it was pulling out of Busang. The U.S. company had also conducted its own test drills and had come up with negligible amounts of gold.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three charities headed by Suharto, and 10 percent each by Hasan and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto.
There has been increasing if veiled criticism of the way in which members of the president's family appear have used their positions to further their now-pervasive business interests.
A government agreement to grant tax and tariff breaks to Suharto's youngest son to produce a "national" car in cooperation with a South Korean firm drew international protests.
Thousands of the cars remain unsold, but Japan has brought the issue before the World Trade Organisation (WTO) for adjudication.
